content.value_statement: Teams need accurate API contracts before documentation, SDKs, and tests can stay aligned. This skill guides OpenAPI 3.1 creation, review, and maintenance for REST APIs.
actual_capabilities: Create OpenAPI 3.1 specs with paths, schemas, responses, servers, and security schemes.
Support design-first, code-first, and hybrid API documentation workflows.
Provide reusable templates for user management APIs and common error responses.
Explain FastAPI and TypeScript annotation patterns for spec generation.
Guide validation, documentation portal setup, and SDK generation workflows.
limitations: Does not execute OpenAPI generators or validators by itself.
Requires users to provide endpoint details, schemas, and authentication rules.
Examples use placeholder domains and sample user resources.
Focuses on REST APIs, not GraphQL or event-driven contracts.

use_cases.title: Design a New API Contract
use_cases.description: Create a clear OpenAPI 3.1 baseline before backend implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Document Existing Endpoints
use_cases.description: Translate route behavior, response models, and validation rules into reusable API documentation.

use_cases.title: Prepare SDK and Portal Inputs
use_cases.description: Refine specs so generated clients and documentation portals have consistent operation details.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new API contract.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a first OpenAPI 3.1 specification for a REST API with these endpoints: [list endpoints]. Include paths, schemas, responses, and authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Draft Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing contract.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OpenAPI draft for missing schemas, weak response definitions, inconsistent operation IDs, and unclear security requirements: [paste summary].

prompt_templates.title: Map Code to OpenAPI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these route definitions and models to propose an OpenAPI 3.1 structure. Identify annotations or metadata needed for generation: [paste routes].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Contract Governance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout for validation and SDK generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow for validating OpenAPI changes, publishing documentation, and generating SDKs. Include checks, ownership, and release steps.

output_examples.input: A team needs a starter contract for user and profile endpoints.
output: A structured API contract outline with resource groups, authentication requirements, and response categories.
A schema plan for users, profiles, pagination, and standard error responses.

output_examples.input: A developer has route handlers but no maintained API documentation.
output: A mapping from routes to operations, parameters, request bodies, and response models.
A checklist for code annotations and validation steps before publishing documentation.

output_examples.input: A documentation owner wants to improve SDK generation quality.
output: A review summary for operation IDs, schema reuse, server entries, and error response consistency.
A release workflow covering spec validation, documentation publishing, and client generation.

best_practices: Start from real endpoint behavior, then normalize names, schemas, and response patterns.
Define authentication, authorization, errors, and pagination consistently across operations.
Validate specs before publishing documentation or generating SDKs.
anti_patterns: Do not leave placeholder schemas in production API contracts.
Do not mix inconsistent operation IDs, tags, and response shapes.
Do not publish specs without documenting security schemes and error formats.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete OpenAPI file?
faq.answer: It can guide the structure and content. The final quality depends on the endpoint details and schemas you provide.

faq.question: Can it work from existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes code-first patterns and helps map routes, models, and annotations to OpenAPI concepts.

faq.question: Does it call external API services?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and examples. It does not make network requests by itself.

faq.question: Which OpenAPI version does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on OpenAPI 3.1, including schemas, reusable components, security schemes, and server metadata.

faq.question: Can it help with SDK generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to prepare consistent specs for client generation and documentation portals.

faq.question: Is it suitable for GraphQL APIs?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on RESTful APIs described with OpenAPI, not GraphQL schemas.
